question: Should OpenClaw core accept signed hosted marketplace feed refresh with local Ed25519 trust anchors and persisted snapshot trust state after the rollback and URL/profile blockers are fixed?
rationale: This PR changes how hosted marketplace content becomes trusted and stored, so automation can identify code blockers but should not approve the trust boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Fix blockers, then approve in stack order
options.body: Repair monotonic signed sequence/freshness handling and URL/profile policy behavior, then land the verifier, config, refresh-state, and visibility slices with explicit maintainer/security approval.

options.title: Request a different trust model
options.body: Ask for changes to key rotation, fail-closed behavior, trust-state shape, or operator rollout before signed refresh enters core.

options.title: Pause signed feed refresh
options.body: Keep the trust stack paused if signed hosted marketplace feed trust is not wanted in OpenClaw core now.

recommendation.title: Fix blockers, then approve in stack order
recommendation.body: Repair monotonic signed sequence/freshness handling and URL/profile policy behavior, then land the verifier, config, refresh-state, and visibility slices with explicit maintainer/security approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the current assignee and authored the live review comments naming the remaining security and compatibility blockers.
